title: Systematic trading enables idea validation through testing
claim: Systematic trading allows testing trading ideas through mathematical models and backtests to validate beliefs about markets, providing evidence before deploying real capital.
support: Author argues systematic approach is key differentiator from discretionary trading; reduces reliance on 'old platitudes and common knowledge'
mechanism: Rigorous testing reveals which market patterns have predictive value and which are false folklore
assumptions: Model rules can be precisely defined
Backtest accurately reflects live trading conditions
validation: Can be validated by comparing backtest assumptions to live execution results

title: Trading models require multiple design decisions with no single correct approach
claim: When constructing backtesting trading strategies, most steps can be done in multiple ways; model design involves choices on data processing, entry/exit rules, risk management, and portfolio construction.
support: Author emphasizes accessibility means focusing on one coherent approach rather than covering all variations; acknowledges multiple valid design patterns
mechanism: Different design choices affect backtest results; requires systematic evaluation of trade-offs
failure_modes: Arbitrary choice leading to data snooping
Inability to generalize across asset classes or regimes
validation: Compare multiple model variants; document design decisions and rationale

title: Portfolio risk depends on diversification and drawdown characteristics
claim: Financial risk in trading portfolios arises from concentration, correlation, and drawdown duration; diversification across asset classes and strategies reduces portfolio-level risk.
support: Standard portfolio theory concept; book emphasizes practical application in strategy design
mechanism: Uncorrelated strategies and assets reduce joint drawdown probability; diversification provides cushion against single-strategy failures
validation: Calculate portfolio drawdown under various correlation assumptions; test vs. individual strategy drawdowns

title: Python environment setup for backtesting requires reproducibility controls
claim: Systematic backtesting frameworks require careful environment setup including Python version pinning, dependency locking, and virtual environments to ensure reproducible results across machines and time.
support: Author emphasizes setup as foundational prerequisite; reproducibility is key testing principle throughout
mechanism: Dependency versions, library API changes, and Python versions affect numerical results and behavior
failure_modes: Dependency drift breaking code over time
Library API changes invalidating old code
validation: Document all environment versions; test reproduction on clean system

title: Python and library versions determine code reproducibility and behavior
claim: Python versions and library versions (pandas, numpy, zipline) have changed significantly since book publication (2021); code examples may produce different results or fail with current versions.
support: Book teaches Python syntax and libraries that evolve; API changes are common in data science ecosystem
mechanism: Numerical precision, function signatures, and default behaviors change across versions
assumptions: Reader will use current versions when following code
Book examples tied to specific historical versions
validation: Test book code examples with current Python/library versions; document breaking changes

title: Pandas is foundational for systematic trading data processing
claim: Pandas library provides efficient tabular data handling, time series operations, and aggregation capabilities essential for financial data processing and backtesting workflows.
support: Book dedicates full chapter to pandas fundamentals; shows data loading, filtering, grouping, and time-based operations
mechanism: Pandas DataFrame structure aligns with financial data (rows=dates, columns=instruments/fields); enables vectorized operations
assumptions: Time index is monotonic and properly labeled
validation: Verify pandas operations produce expected outputs on sample data

title: Backtesting requires controlled simulation of order execution and fill assumptions
claim: Backtesting trading strategies requires explicit simulation of entry/exit logic, position sizing, commission costs, slippage assumptions, and order fill behavior to realistically model live performance.
support: Core chapter on backtesting framework; discusses zipline framework and custom implementations
mechanism: Differences between backtest and live execution (slippage, commissions, margin availability, liquidity constraints) cause performance divergence
assumptions: Historical bars are sufficient for entry/exit
Commission and slippage assumptions are accurate
Margin and liquidity constraints are known
failure_modes: Ignoring liquidity constraints on large positions
validation: Compare backtest parameters to live execution; measure realized slippage vs. backtest assumptions

title: Backtest result analysis requires multiple performance metrics and risk measures
claim: Analyzing backtest results requires comprehensive metrics including Sharpe ratio, maximum drawdown, return distribution, win rate, profit factor, and statistical significance tests to characterize strategy performance and robustness.
support: Dedicated chapter on metric selection; emphasizes avoiding single-metric optimization that can lead to spurious findings
mechanism: Different metrics reveal different aspects: Sharpe (risk-adjusted return), drawdown (capital preservation), profit factor (edge consistency), win rate (trade frequency)
assumptions: Returns are normally distributed or have known distribution
Metrics are computed over sufficient sample
failure_modes: Insufficient sample size for statistical validity
validation: Compute metrics on independent out-of-sample data; verify consistency of metrics across periods

title: Exchange-traded funds (ETFs) provide convenient diversified exposure to market segments
claim: ETFs are financial instruments providing diversified, liquid, low-cost exposure to asset classes, sectors, or themes; suitable for systematic trend-following and momentum strategies.
support: Explains ETF structure, costs, and advantages vs. mutual funds; discusses ETF selection criteria
mechanism: ETF expense ratios and bid-ask spreads affect net returns; correlation structure enables diversification
assumptions: Liquidity is sufficient for strategy entry/exit
validation: Compare ETF performance vs. index; verify tracking error assumptions

title: Systematic ETF model construction combines asset selection with risk management
claim: ETF-based systematic models combine universe selection (which ETFs), momentum/trend signals (entry rules), and portfolio construction (position sizing, rebalancing frequency) to build diversified equity strategies.
support: Book shows complete worked example of ETF momentum strategy design and backtesting
mechanism: ETF selection reduces evaluation set; momentum signals identify strong performers; rebalancing manages correlation drift
assumptions: Rebalancing frequency balances frictional costs vs. signal freshness
validation: Backtest ETF model on multiple time periods; verify statistical significance

title: Systematic momentum is a quantifiable entry/exit signal based on recent price trends
claim: Momentum strategies generate entry signals when asset prices have recently outperformed and exit signals when momentum weakens; can be implemented as trend-following (long momentum) or mean-reversion (short momentum).
support: Extensive worked examples showing momentum calculation (lookback periods), signal generation, and portfolio construction
mechanism: Momentum reflects underlying price trends; trend continuation is observed in multiple time frames and asset classes
assumptions: Signal generation rules are well-defined and implementable
failure_modes: Lookback period too short or too long
Momentum signals occurring at trend reversals
validation: Backtest momentum signals on out-of-sample data; verify return predictability of momentum scores

title: Trend-following on futures uses volatility-adjusted position sizing and trend signals
claim: Futures trend-following strategies use volatility estimates to scale position size, apply trend filters (e.g., moving average crossovers) to determine direction, and manage risk through stop losses or volatility bands.
support: Detailed implementation of trend-following strategy on commodity and financial futures; discusses specific indicators and risk management
mechanism: Volatility-adjusted sizing equalizes risk across assets; trend filters reduce whipsaws; stop losses limit individual trade losses
failure_modes: Trend filter lag causing late entries/exits
validation: Backtest trend-following parameters over multiple commodity/futures markets and time periods

title: Combining models requires understanding correlation and diversification benefits
claim: Combining multiple trading models (strategies on different assets or different signal types) reduces portfolio drawdown when strategies are uncorrelated; diversification benefit is proportional to correlation structure.
support: Shows correlation matrix analysis and portfolio optimization for model combination; demonstrates drawdown reduction from diversification
mechanism: Uncorrelated strategies fail independently; joint drawdown is less than sum of individual drawdowns
assumptions: Equal weighting or optimization produces acceptable results
validation: Compute realized correlation and portfolio drawdown vs. expectations; test on multiple time periods

title: Performance visualization aids strategy comparison and decision making
claim: Visualizing cumulative returns, drawdown curves, monthly heatmaps, and correlation matrices helps compare strategies, identify regime changes, and communicate results to stakeholders.
support: Shows code examples for matplotlib and pandas plotting; demonstrates value of multi-perspective visualization
mechanism: Visual patterns reveal insights not obvious in summary statistics (e.g., regime changes, seasonality, drawdown clustering)
assumptions: Visual patterns generalize to future periods
validation: Compare visualizations to summary statistics; verify insights from visualization

title: Statistical significance testing prevents false discoveries from data snooping
claim: Testing many strategies on historical data risks finding false patterns that don't persist forward (data snooping bias); statistical significance tests and out-of-sample validation are required to avoid spurious findings.

source.section: You can't beat all of the Monkeys all of the Time

support: Chapter dedicated to statistical pitfalls; discusses multiple comparisons problem, optimism bias, and overfitting risks
mechanism: Random testing produces false positives; larger test set increases false discovery rate; p-hacking amplifies problem
validation: Apply rigorous hypothesis testing; validate on truly independent out-of-sample data; report all tests performed

title: Data sourcing and import are critical for backtesting accuracy and reproducibility
claim: Systematic backtesting requires careful data sourcing (choosing reliable vendors), data validation (checking for gaps, errors, corporate actions), and clean import processes to ensure data quality throughout the pipeline.
support: Dedicated chapter on practical data handling; discusses common pitfalls like survivorship bias, corporate actions, data quality issues
mechanism: Poor data quality corrupts backtest results; biased data sources produce misleading performance estimates
failure_modes: Stale or non-real-time pricing in backtests
validation: Validate data integrity (gaps, duplicates); compare to vendor documentation; verify corporate action adjustments

title: Futures provide leveraged exposure enabling portfolio diversification and tail hedging
claim: Futures contracts on commodities and financial indexes provide liquid, low-cost leveraged exposure; systematic futures strategies can complement equity portfolios for diversification and hedge portfolio drawdowns.
support: Book explains futures structure, contract specifications, and advantages vs. direct commodity exposure
mechanism: Futures correlate differently than equities to macroeconomic factors; trend-following on commodities often provides negative correlation to equity drawdowns
assumptions: Leverage is available on reasonable terms
Contract roll mechanics don't cause undue friction
validation: Compare equity+futures portfolio drawdown vs. equity-only; verify correlation assumptions

title: Futures backtesting requires modeling contract roll mechanics and cost impacts
claim: Systematic backtesting of futures strategies must explicitly model contract roll points (switching from front contract to next contract), handling date discontinuities, roll slippage, and time decay effects.
support: Practical guidance on handling futures-specific data issues in backtests
mechanism: Futures contracts expire; continuous series requires synthetic splicing at roll points; roll slippage and term structure effects impact returns
assumptions: Roll mechanics can be simulated accurately
Term structure doesn't dramatically change across periods
failure_modes: Unrealistic roll simulation causing spurious returns
Naive contract splicing causing price discontinuities
validation: Verify contract roll timing and slippage against historical data; compare to live execution

title: Database design enables efficient historical data retrieval and backtesting at scale
claim: Systematic trading at scale requires database design (indexing strategies, time-series optimization) and data management practices to efficiently retrieve historical data and enable reproducible backtesting workflows.
support: Practical guidance on database selection, indexing for time-based queries, and data organization
mechanism: Proper indexing reduces query time; partitioning by date/instrument balances storage and retrieval efficiency
failure_modes: Inefficient queries causing runtime performance issues
validation: Benchmark query performance; verify data consistency; profile database load
